title: Vision Board: what it is, where it's at, where it's going
summary: My reading of the project from docs/vision.md, the tracker and the board-v3 task status (2026-10-06). Acknowledge what I got right, drop what's wrong, comment to correct me. This is also the first real use of the board by an agent with only the MCP tools (tracker N17).

node.title: The bottleneck is taking in AI output, not producing it
node.body: AI produces a lot quickly. What slows us down is absorbing it well enough to make the next decision.

node.title: Text replies don't scale to dozens of points
node.body: A big piece of work comes back as findings, risks, options and questions. Answering each one in chat means quoting it back. Numbered lists help ("1 ok, 4 skip") but stay a wall of text.

node.title: People become conductors
node.body: As the agent does more of the work, the person steers. Steering needs a visual surface to decide from, item by item.

node.title: Works on any project, not only code
node.body: Code, product, writing, research: anything an agent can investigate. Chat stays the default; the board is for when the output is too big for text.

node.title: 1. Agent draws
node.body: The agent describes nodes, links and containers through one API (HTTP, `vb` CLI or MCP). It never writes coordinates; the layout engine places everything.

node.title: 2. Person reviews
node.body: Acknowledge, drop, comment, ask for more context, or save for later. Lasso a group and pin one note. Every item has a stable number.

node.title: 3. Agent reads back
node.body: The agent reads the answers (`check_responses`) and must answer every flagged item: a reply, a redraw, or a proposal the person decides.

node.title: 4. Board moves on
node.body: A new version of each changed card. The person re-reads only what changed, and decisions leave the open set.

node.title: One ledger per project, many chats
node.body: Everything goes into one append-only ledger (`.visionboard/ledger.jsonl`). Each container is a thread of work owned by one chat. Any chat can read everything; writing to another chat's container needs the person's grant.

node.title: Project ledger and fold
node.body: Append-only ledger, format v7, with schema validation. The board is worked out from it (U3 step 1).

node.title: Board API: HTTP, vb, MCP
node.body: OpenAPI is the single source; the routes, `vb` commands, MCP tools and reference docs are generated from it and tested for drift. **Awaiting your review (U4).**

node.title: Cards and containers
node.body: `<vb-node>`, `<vb-region>`, Markdown bodies, no overlaps, icon row, note bubbles beside cards (Stages 2a to 2e).

node.title: Selection and moving
node.body: Select and drag, Shift+drag lasso, selection bar, group notes, zoom, moving cards between containers, the Later container, container notes (Stage 3, done 2026-10-06).

node.title: Card width adapts to content
node.body: S/M/L sizes behind the `nodeSize` flag (D-030). **Awaiting your review (U7).**

node.title: Incremental updates
node.body: Only changed cards and their containers redraw, with per-container layout (N12).

node.title: First real use (N17)
node.body: An agent with only the MCP tools and "communicate with me through the board". This board is that test.

node.title: Then write the agent skill
node.body: Interview you, then write when and how an agent uses the board (which layout for what, when to ask), based on what real use showed.

node.title: Send, proposals, seen, parking
node.body: Board v3 Stages 4 and 5: a Send button, the agent proposes and the person decides, seen badges, park bundles for picking work up in a new chat.

node.title: Chat panel on the board
node.body: Stage 6: a chat panel on the right, MCP first, then kiro-cli (D-010). Ends the copy-paste workaround (W3).

node.title: Person edits and purge
node.body: N11: the person edits a card's text as a new version. N14: remove and purge a sent note, the one exception to append-only.

node.title: Versions, Confirm these, Approve
node.body: From Uplynk Architect: change highlights, an assumptions list to confirm, an approved version as the working decision (M1).

node.title: More layout modes, cleaner connectors
node.body: Tree, timeline, matrix, layers, text (L1); connectors that route around cards (M2).

node.title: A skill or plugin in any agent session
node.body: The end state: any agent session can open a board. Perhaps hosted one day (L3), and patterns shared back to Uplynk (L2).

node.title: Did I get the core idea right?
node.body: If one card above is off, comment on it. If the whole framing is off, comment here.

node.title: How should other chats join?
node.body: You want to use the board from another chat. The MCP server is set up per project in `~/.claude.json`. Options: add `vb` to that other project's config, or start a new chat here. Which project is it?

node.title: Workaround W1 looks resolved
node.body: The tracker says `/usr/local/bin/node` is 22.14 and can't run `.ts`. Today it reports v24.14.0, and the MCP server runs on it. Drop W1?

node.title: U4 and U7 are waiting on your review
node.body: Board API (U4) and card width (U7) were built 2026-10-05. Review them next, or keep going with real use?

title: nclite harnesses: Codex + Claude CLI update
summary: Two lanes. Left: bring OpenAI Codex in as a second harness. Right: move the bundled Claude Code CLI off its August pin. Each lane runs top to bottom; answer the numbered items.

region.title: Lane B: Claude Code CLI update

node.title: Where we are
node.body:
- Image pins Claude Code **2.1.229** (picked 13 Aug, the fast `latest` channel)
- npm latest today is **2.1.295**, 66 releases on
- Pinned in 2 live places: `container/Dockerfile`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (IMAGE-NOTICES regenerates itself)
- About 20 comments/docs say "measured on 2.1.229"
- No bump checklist exists; N189 asked for one and it was never written
- `npm test` never runs the real CLI. Only the skills probe in `rebuild-agent.sh` does

node.title: 1. Research: changelog 2.1.229 → 2.1.295
node.body:
Read the release notes for anything touching what we rely on:
- flags and stream-json events
- hooks (exit 2 blocks, stderr reaches model, inline `--settings` merge)
- compaction settings and env vars
- `claude auth login/status` text
- bundled skills, tool ids (`Task`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`)
- install.cjs / platform package split
Output: a short result file listing likely breaks.

node.title: Which channel do we pin from?
node.body:
- **latest** (fast): what we did in August, most fixes, most churn
- **stable** tag: lags behind, fewer surprises
Recommend: stable, unless the changelog shows a fix we need that only latest has.

node.title: 2. Write the CLI bump checklist
node.body:
Turn the re-verify list into one repeatable doc, so the next bump is routine:
- every pin site
- every version-sensitive behaviour + how to test it spend-free
- closes the gap N189 named

node.title: 3. Terms check for the new version
node.body: Licence text, package layout, notices. Same check as the August bundling research (N156, U47 context). N156 itself stays open.

node.title: 4. Bump + rebuild image
node.body:
- Edit Dockerfile pin and its comment
- `scripts/rebuild-agent.sh` → next tag (0.1.35 → 0.1.36)
- build fails early if `claude --version` breaks
- skills probe must pass before `DEFAULT_IMAGE` moves

node.title: 5. Verify inside the image (no spend)
node.body:
Against the stand-in vendor:
- turn args + stream-json events + `system/init` tool list
- read gate blocks a read (exit 2)
- compaction settings respected
- transcript path layout
- sign-in / signed-out strings
- web search tool ids
- bundled skills off

node.title: 6. Model-switch experiment
node.body: Re-check that the CLI still drops another model's signed thinking and retries (N186, N189). This is why switching models mid-chat is safe today.

node.title: 7. Notices, docs, bundle, commit
node.body:
- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` by hand
- re-date the "measured on" comments that were re-measured
- `scripts/runtime-bundle.sh`
- commit

node.title: Risk: we match the CLI's own words
node.body:
- `signInRefused` matches two exact sentences
- `isWrongSessionFlag` matches loose text
- read gate relies on the stderr format
66 releases is plenty of time for any of these to change wording. Step 5 must hit each one.

region.title: Lane A: Codex as a harness

node.title: Where we are
node.body:
- **Nothing built.** Research only: CONDITIONAL GO (29 Aug), TRACKER N57 + L2, both parked post-launch
- Research measured Codex **0.151.0**; latest is **0.162.0**
- The 15 follow-up checks (O-1..O-15) were handed over, then archived as "completed" on 7 Sep without being worked
- Since then 3 got easier: our sign-in design (vendor's own CLI inside the wall) replaces host-side token refresh (O-6), key injection is settled (O-7), UI types are generated (O-9)
- Ready to plug into: `HarnessDriver` + `DRIVERS`, `buildRunArgs`, the Anthropic relay as a template, egress tickets, the subscription seam ("one file beside claude.ts")

node.title: 1. Re-probe on 0.162.0
node.body:
Re-run the open checks before any code. The ones that can kill the design:
- O-5 real MCP tool timeout vs our approval wait
- O-10 Codex obeys `HTTPS_PROXY` (egress wall)
- O-13 why it calls chatgpt.com / github.com
- O-2 event shapes, O-11 exit codes, O-14 Linux deps
- O-1 Ollama/ZAI speak `/v1/responses`
Output: updated result doc, each item closed or not.

node.title: API key first, or ChatGPT sign-in first?
node.body:
- **API key first**: no terms question, credential path already proven (`env_key = NCLITE_RUN_TOKEN`)
- **ChatGPT sign-in first**: the reason we want Codex (more ChatGPT users), but needs OpenAI terms checked and chatgpt.com through the wall
Recommend: API key first, sign-in as the very next slice.

node.title: Who checks OpenAI's terms for ChatGPT sign-in?
node.body: No terms analysis exists. Claude's case rests on "unmodified vendor CLI, user's own login". Whether OpenAI allows the same is not established. Same shape as the Anthropic question (N156).

node.title: Accept these Codex differences?
node.body:
- `view_image` and multi-agent can't be switched off → always on, with a warning
- Codex reads `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills` from the workspace every turn, so a file the bot writes becomes next turn's instructions
- Replies arrive as whole blocks, not typed out live (live needs the experimental app-server)
Accept all three for v1, or which need a fix?

node.title: One image or two?
node.body:
Codex adds about 300 MB.
- **One image**: simpler, every install pays the size
- **Separate codex image**: smaller default, a second build and bundle to keep
Recommend: one image, re-measure after 0.162.0.

node.title: 2. Names: harness + vendor kind
node.body:
- add `codex` to `HARNESSES` (engine) and the container's list
- an `openai` vendor kind (today reserved and refused) with a Responses dialect
- base template tool defaults for codex

node.title: 3. Responses relay
node.body:
New `/api/run/openai/v1/responses` on the run door, modelled on the Anthropic relay:
- streams through
- strips `x-codex-*` headers (they leak the workspace path and git hash)
- the container only ever holds the run token

node.title: 4. codexDriver
node.body:
Host-side adapter in `DRIVERS`:
- config passed only by `-c`, plus `--strict-config`, `--ignore-user-config`
- our tools via MCP, Codex's own shell off
- tool timeout ≥ the approval wait (≥900s, to prove in step 1)
- agent dir + skills mounts

node.title: 5. Container adapter
node.body:
`container/harness-codex.ts`, one `codex exec --json` per turn, copied from the Claude one:
- chat → Codex thread id map
- turn timeout, cap on failing tools, dedupe on retry
- clear message when a turn ends with nothing said

node.title: 6. Into the image
node.body:
- install Codex pinned, notices, size measured
- add to `HARNESS_CLIS`, bundled-skills off + probe
- fix `container/README.md` (still says harnesses arrive as ACP adapters; research rejected that)

node.title: 7. Verify end to end
node.body:
- a turn through the relay with no spend
- an approval that waits past 60s and still lands
- egress wall holds, no stray hosts
- then a few real turns (prompts are code)

node.title: 8. UI: pick Codex
node.body: Harness choice in the preset, OpenAI entry in add-a-model. Reuse existing components; mock-up first.

node.title: 9. ChatGPT sign-in slice
node.body: One file beside `claude.ts` in the subscription seam. Needs chatgpt.com through the wall, Codex's device sign-in in the container, and the terms answer.

node.title: Risk: approval wait vs Codex tool timeout
node.body: Codex gives up on a tool after 60s by default. Our approval waits 120s (up to 600s). Untested fix: raise the timeout. If it doesn't hold, the bot fails every slow approval.

node.title: Risk: Codex config fails open
node.body:
- a misplaced config key silently sends traffic to the real api.openai.com
- an unreachable endpoint retries forever
- an unknown tool name looped 999+ times
Guarded by `--strict-config` and the adapter caps in step 5.
